blurb: Speech recognition, text-to-speech, real-time voice assistants and the risks of cloned voices.

cards.title: From sound waves to words

steps.p: Audio is converted into a spectrogram: how much energy is at each frequency, over time.
A transformer encoder processes the spectrogram frames, much as a vision model processes image patches.
A decoder generates the transcript token by token, attending to the encoded audio.

cards.aside: OpenAI's Whisper (2022) uses exactly this encoder-decoder design.

cards.q: OpenAI trained Whisper on roughly how much transcribed audio?
cards.why: About 680,000 hours. The transcripts were imperfect, scraped from the web, but sheer scale and variety made Whisper robust to accents and noise.

cards.statement: Most speech models read the raw audio waveform directly as their input.
cards.why: Mostly false. Many, including Whisper, use log-Mel spectrograms, a compact representation of frequency content. Some self-supervised models do learn from raw waveforms.

options: How strong each frequency is at each moment
cards.why: Frequency vs time. Vowels show up as horizontal bands, consonants as bursts, and silence as dark gaps.

cards.title: OpenAI released Whisper's model weights openly in September 2022.
cards.detail: It can also translate speech from many languages directly into English text. Open weights made it a building block for countless transcription apps.

cards.statement: A speech recognizer's word error rate can exceed 100%.
cards.why: True. WER counts substitutions, deletions and insertions relative to the reference length. A system that inserts lots of extra words can go above 100%.

cards.title: How text-to-speech evolved

steps.p: Early systems glued together snippets of recorded speech, which sounded choppy.
DeepMind's WaveNet (2016) generated audio one sample at a time, producing strikingly natural voices.
Neural audio codecs compress sound into discrete tokens, so language-model techniques can generate speech.

cards.aside: Modern TTS can convey emotion, pacing and even laughter.

cards.q: To capture sound frequencies up to 8 kHz, you must sample audio at least…
cards.why: 16 kHz — twice the highest frequency. That is the Nyquist rule. 16 kHz is standard for speech; CDs use 44.1 kHz to cover the whole range of human hearing.

cards.q: Neural audio codecs like SoundStream and EnCodec convert audio into…
cards.why: Audio tokens. Once speech is a token sequence, a transformer can predict it like text, enabling voice cloning, music generation and speech-to-speech models.

cards.statement: Modern voice cloning can imitate a voice from just a few seconds of audio.
cards.why: True. Microsoft's VALL-E (2023) reported cloning from a three-second sample. Commercial tools now offer similar abilities.

cards.title: WaveNet initially needed so much computation that generating one second of speech took far longer than a second.
cards.detail: Producing tens of thousands of samples one by one was slow. Later techniques made it fast enough that Google deployed WaveNet voices in its Assistant in 2017.

cards.q: What made WaveNet's voices sound so much more natural than older systems?
options: It generated the raw waveform directly with a neural network
cards.why: Direct waveform modeling. Instead of stitching or vocoding, it learned the fine structure of real speech sample by sample.

cards.title: Cascaded vs native

steps.p: Classic assistants chain three models: speech recognition, a language model, then text-to-speech. Each adds delay.
Converting to text throws away tone, emotion, laughter and background sounds.
Native audio models hear and speak directly, responding faster and handling interruptions more naturally.

cards.aside: Turn-taking timing is what makes a voice assistant feel human or robotic.

cards.q: In human conversation, the typical gap between one person finishing and the other starting is about…
cards.why: About 200 ms, found consistently across many languages. We start planning replies before the other person finishes, which assistants struggle to match.

cards.statement: Cascaded voice pipelines lose information such as tone of voice.
cards.why: True. Once speech becomes text, sarcasm, hesitation or distress in the voice is gone unless separately detected.

cards.q: Voice activity detection in an assistant decides…
options: When the user has started or stopped speaking
cards.why: Turn boundaries. Too eager and it interrupts mid-pause; too cautious and responses feel sluggish.

cards.title: Some voice models are "full-duplex": they can listen and talk at the same time.
cards.detail: Like people, they can handle interruptions and small listener cues such as "mm-hmm" while speaking, rather than strictly taking turns.

cards.q: The biggest latency win from speech-to-speech models comes from…
options: Skipping separate transcription and synthesis stages
cards.why: Removing handoffs. Each stage in a cascade waits for the previous one. One model can begin responding almost immediately.

cards.title: Generative audio grows up

steps.p: Systems like Suno and Udio generate full songs with vocals from a short text description.
In 2024, major record labels sued Suno and Udio, alleging they trained on copyrighted recordings without permission.
Cloned voices have been used in scams and political disinformation.

cards.aside: Audio is especially persuasive because people trust familiar voices.

cards.q: Who sued AI music companies Suno and Udio in 2024?
options: Major record labels, coordinated by the RIAA
cards.why: The major labels — Universal, Sony and Warner — through the Recording Industry Association of America, alleging copyright infringement in training.

cards.title: In 2024, a robocall faked President Biden's voice to tell New Hampshire voters not to vote.
cards.detail: Soon after, the US Federal Communications Commission ruled that AI-generated voices in robocalls fall under existing restrictions on artificial voices, making such calls illegal without consent.

cards.statement: Scammers have used cloned voices to impersonate family members asking for money.
cards.why: True. Consumer protection agencies have warned about calls in which a cloned voice of a relative claims an emergency and asks for urgent payment.

cards.q: What is a simple, effective defense against voice-clone scams in a family?
options: Agree on a private code word to confirm identity in emergencies
cards.why: A shared secret. A cloner can copy a voice but not a word you never said online. Hanging up and calling back on a known number also works.

cards.title: Set a family code word
cards.body: A pre-agreed word lets you verify a frantic call in seconds. It costs nothing and defeats even a perfect voice clone.
cards.challenge: Message your family today and agree on a code word for emergency calls.
